target.title: fix(agents): detect bundled and legacy providers in model-not-found hint
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a bundled provider or a legacy `openai-codex` provider has no authenticated profile or no registered model, the runtime error prescribes a `models.providers[]` config entry that the config validator rejects without `baseUrl`, creating contradictory guidance and a gateway crash-loop.

- **Problem**: `buildMissingProviderModelRegistrationHint` unconditionally suggests adding a `models.providers[]` entry, even for bundled providers whose models register automatically at startup. For the legacy `openai-codex` alias, this is doubly harmful: the config validator rejects the overlay, bricking the gateway.
- **Solution**: Add two early-return checks before the generic config-entry suggestion — one for all bundled providers (via `isBuiltInModelProviderOverlayId`), one for the legacy `openai-codex` alias (via `normalizeProviderId`). Each points operators to the correct recovery path.
- **What changed**: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.ts` (new logic in `buildMissingProviderModelRegistrationHint` + import), `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts` (updated 1 test, added 2 new tests)
- **What did NOT change**: Config validator behavior; `BUILT_IN_MODEL_PROVIDER_OVERLAY_IDS` set; non-bundled/custom provider hint path; `agentRuntimeId` hint path; doctor migration code

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #100066
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The issue reporter followed the runtime's error message verbatim and ended up with a gateway that would not boot. The root cause is that the hint function doesn't account for bundled providers (whose models are registered automatically) or legacy aliases (which should be migrated via doctor). Both paths need different recovery instructions than the generic "add a models.providers[] entry" advice.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Error message guidance for bundled provider and legacy openai-codex model-not-found errors
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.19+, `fix/bundled-provider-auth-hint-100066` branch, OpenClaw local checkout
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
# Run production resolveModelAsync with skipAgentDiscovery
pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

- Evidence after fix:

The tests exercise the production code path (`resolveModelAsync`) with `createRuntimeHooks()`. Each test calls the same function that the gateway uses at runtime, confirming the exact error message text for each scenario.

```console
$ pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose

 ✓ suggests checking auth when a bundled provider model entry is missing
 ✓ suggests running doctor for legacy openai-codex provider
 ✓ suggests adding config entry when a non-bundled provider model is missing

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  122 passed (122)
```

Actual error messages produced by `resolveModelAsync` (verified by test assertions):

```console
# Bundled provider (microsoft-foundry/Kimi-K2.6-1):
Unknown model: microsoft-foundry/Kimi-K2.6-1. Found agents.defaults.models["microsoft-foundry/Kimi-K2.6-1"], but the bundled provider "microsoft-foundry" has no registered model "Kimi-K2.6-1". This usually means the provider has no authenticated profile — run `openclaw models status` to check provider auth and re-authenticate if needed. See https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-providers.

# Legacy openai-codex (openai-codex/gpt-5.4):
Unknown model: openai-codex/gpt-5.4. Found agents.defaults.models["openai-codex/gpt-5.4"], but "openai-codex" is a legacy provider ID. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to migrate to the current OpenAI provider format. If the provider has no authenticated profile, run `openclaw models status` to check provider auth and re-authenticate if needed. See https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-providers.

# Custom provider (custom-provider/some-model - unchanged):
Unknown model: custom-provider/some-model. Found agents.defaults.models["custom-provider/some-model"], but no matching models.providers["custom-provider"].models[] entry. Add { "id": "some-model", "name": "some-model" } to models.providers["custom-provider"].models[] to register this provider model. For custom or proxy providers, also set api and baseUrl so requests route to the intended endpoint. See https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-providers.
```

Before/after matrix:

| Input | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|-------|:---:|:---:|
| `microsoft-foundry/Kimi-K2.6-1` (bundled) | `"...no matching models.providers["microsoft-foundry"].models[] entry. Add { "id": "Kimi-K2.6-1", "name": "Kimi-K2.6-1" }..."` | `"...the bundled provider "microsoft-foundry" has no registered model "Kimi-K2.6-1". This usually means the provider has no authenticated profile — run \`openclaw models status\`..."` |
| `openai-codex/gpt-5.4` (legacy) | `"...no matching models.providers["openai-codex"].models[] entry. Add { "id": "gpt-5.4", "name": "gpt-5.4" }..."` | `""openai-codex" is a legacy provider ID. Run \`openclaw doctor --fix\` to migrate to the current OpenAI provider format..."` |
| `custom-provider/some-model` (non-bundled) | `"...no matching models.providers["custom-provider"].models[] entry..."` | **Unchanged** (same as before) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Bundled providers (`microsoft-foundry`) now show auth-check guidance instead of config-entry advice
  2. Legacy `openai-codex` now shows doctor migration + auth guidance
  3. Non-bundled providers (`custom-provider`) retain the config-entry guidance (unchanged)
  4. All 122 tests pass, including 3 covering the bundled/legacy/custom paths
- What was not tested: Full gateway startup with a bundled provider lacking auth (requires Docker orchestration, out of scope for error message change); existing real-world configs with `openai-codex` model refs (already handled by `openclaw doctor --fix`)

## Root Cause

`buildMissingProviderModelRegistrationHint` (introduced in `1ee2733b2f`, Vincent Koc, 2026-06-17) lacked awareness of bundled provider model registration and legacy provider alias migration. The function always fell through to the generic `models.providers[]` config-entry suggestion, which the config validator rejects for non-built-in provider overlay ids without `baseUrl`.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Operators encountering model-not-found errors for bundled providers will now see actionable guidance pointing to the actual cause (missing auth or legacy migration) instead of misleading config instructions that crash the gateway.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only error message text changes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix is at the shared hint function entry point, covering all callers. The two-layer approach (generic `isBuiltInModelProviderOverlayId` + specific `openai-codex` check) covers both bundled providers and legacy aliases without modifying the validator or the `BUILT_IN_MODEL_PROVIDER_OVERLAY_IDS` set.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The change is focused and minimal.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding `openai-codex` to `BUILT_IN_MODEL_PROVIDER_OVERLAY_IDS` — rejected because repository policy treats `openai-codex` as legacy-only input, not a valid new provider overlay.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes (Claude Code)
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Deep analysis of competing PRs #100086 and #100104, identification of blind spots in both, layered fix design

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Operators who previously relied on the misleading config-entry hint to add a `models.providers[]` entry for a bundled provider will now see different guidance. Mitigation: The new guidance points to the correct recovery path (auth check or doctor migration), and the old path was causing a gateway crash-loop, so any change is an improvement.

No compatibility risk — only error message text changes, no runtime behavior modification.
